literal: If one removes the painful disease called hostility, it will give a glory without decrease and without decay.
translation: If a person rids themselves of the painful disease called hostility, it will bring them an endless and undecaying glory.
modern: பகைமை என்று சொல்லப்படும் துன்பம் தரும் நோயை ஒருவன் நீக்கினால், அது அவனுக்குக் குறைவில்லாத, அழிவில்லாத புகழைக் கொடுக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the immense benefit of overcoming hostility. The poet metaphorically describes hostility as a painful disease ('எவ்வநோய்') because of the constant mental and social suffering it inflicts. If one manages to cure or remove this disease, it yields a life of great glory ('விளக்கம்'). This resulting glory is described as endless ('தவலில்லா') and free from any decay or blemish ('தாவில்').
